newsitem.title: UK: Analysts see 78p-90p/shr for Sears break-up.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see 78p-90p/shr for Sears break-up.

text.p: British retailer Sears Plc's break-up will be clouded by uncertainty about the cost of ditching its loss-making British Shoe Corporation, retail analysts said on Tuesday.

Analysts said different views on the cost of exiting BSC, the value of flagship department store Selfridges and the clothing businesses, accounted for a wide range of break-up valuations, ranging from 78 to 90 pence a share. They doubted Sears could get rid of BSC at no cost and estimated it could mean a 150 to 200 million stg hit.
The break-up aims to add value for Sears' shareholders, but doubts about the cost of rationalising BSC are overshadowing the potential benefits.
"There's a lot of uncertainty attached to the upside, that's why the shares are not moving," said one retail analyst.
Sears earlier announced break-up plans, including the demerger of Selfridges. Its shares were unchanged at 77.5 pence at 1425 GMT.
Analysts' break-up valuation estimates included a 25 pence a share payout from the 367.5 million stg sale of Freemans mail the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.

"The risks on the break up are is that the MMC could block the Freemans deal, plus uncertainty about the cost of BSC and the valuation of Selfridges, which won't be demerged until 1998," said another retail analyst.
Some said Selfridges could be worth as much as 600 million stg, while other analysts doubted even a potential purchaser would want to pay this much and suggested a more conservative 500 million.
Sears' chairman Sir Bob Reid said earlier on Tuesday he believed the department store was worth considerably more than 600 million stg.
The clothing businesses, including Wallis, Warehouse and Miss Selfridge, could be worth around 400 million stg, according to one analyst, who declined to be identified.
Analysts said valuing the rump of Sears - womenswear plus BSC, obviously depended on the fate of BSC. "One should assume a big negative to get out of all or part of BSC," said another analyst.
"Obviously everyone's going to hope this company doctor David James (the new head of BSC) is going to manage something better," the analyst said.
Forecasts for Sears 1997/98 results were downgraded in the light of its report on current trading. One analyst said he was cutting his to 70 million stg from 85 million previously.
